quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 40 Questions • Passing Score 35

questions.question: Riding at night:

options.text: Is not recommended.
Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
Is not safe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.
Should only be done in the city.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials when riding at night. This makes you more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: When riding in the rain, you should:

options.text: Ride down the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.
questions.explanation: Roads become very slippery when rain first starts. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars to get better grip.

questions.question: When riding at night instead of during the day, a motorcycle rider should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Ride more slowly.
Keep more space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
Use your high beam whenever possible.
Follow other vehicles too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow other vehicles too closely.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes when riding at night, slow down and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Change your lane position as needed, especially at night.

questions.question: This sign warns you of:

options.text: A right turn.
An intersection.
A lane change.
A road curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: An intersection.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a T intersection is ahead.

questions.question: The best lane position for a motorcycle:

options.text: Is on the left side of the lane, next to the centerline.
Is on the right side of the lane, next to the curb.
Depends on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Depends on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: The best lane position changes based on the situation. Choose the position that gives you the best view and most space around you. Move to a different position as traffic changes.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should tell them to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after you start the engine.
Sit as close to the front as possible without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Talk whenever they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk whenever they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should not talk or move around too much so you can focus on riding. Tell passengers to board only after the engine starts. They should sit as close to the front as possible without crowding you and hold firmly to your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Before riding, check all of the following, except:

options.text: Your tire pressure.
The tread depth on your tires.
How reflective your tires are.
The condition of your tire sidewalls.

questions.correctAnswerText: How reflective your tires are.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tire pressure, tread depth, and the general condition of your tire sidewalls and tread.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Yield when turning left on a green light.
One-way traffic.
Cattle crossing.
Two-way left turn lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield when turning left on a green light.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that when turning left at a green light, they must yield to oncoming traffic and only complete the turn when it is safe.

questions.question: An advantage of keeping a motorcycle group small is:

options.text: A small group is less likely to get separated by traffic.
A small group can break traffic laws to stay together.
Riders will always be trying to catch up to the group.
It will be hard to keep track of where everyone is.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small group is less likely to get separated by traffic.
questions.explanation: Small groups have several advantages over large groups. Other vehicles can pass them more easily, traffic and stop lights are less likely to separate them, and slower riders do not have to rush to catch up.

questions.question: When a tire goes flat, you can usually hear it.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire go flat. Instead, you will notice a sudden change in how your motorcycle handles.

questions.question: What is a linked braking system?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes work when you use either brake lever.
It connects the front brake to the gear shifter so the brake applies when you downshift.
It connects the rear brake to a foot control.
It connects the rear brake to a handlebar switch.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes work when you use either brake lever.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake lever, both brakes apply pressure. Read your owner's manual to learn more about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: What should you do about mirror checks?

options.text: They are not important.
Do them only on long trips.
Do them regularly as part of normal riding.
They don't help because you can't change what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do them regularly as part of normal riding.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal riding routine. Also check your mirrors before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other—either brake then swerve or swerve then brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other—either brake then swerve or swerve then brake.
questions.explanation: When you must brake and swerve, do these actions separately, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: When should you do head checks?

options.text: Only when changing lanes.
Only when turning.
Rarely, because looking around takes your eyes off the road ahead.
Often, as part of your normal riding routine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often, as part of your normal riding routine.
questions.explanation: Do head checks frequently as part of your normal riding routine. Knowing what is happening around you helps you be prepared for any situation.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Use the front brake only.
Use the front brake first.
Slow down the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both the front and rear brakes together at the same time.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Only use your mirrors to check for other vehicles.
Turn your head to look for traffic behind you.
Do not worry about other traffic.
Brake hard to let any vehicles in your blind spot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to look for traffic behind you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like cars. Always turn your head to check for traffic before you change lanes.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Steep hill ahead.
The road ahead has turns or curves.
The road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert drivers to possible dangers. This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when wet and is harder to drive safely on.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder.
Use the left side of your lane.
Use the center of your lane.
Use the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, riding in the center of your lane is safest. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to return to your lane too soon, which is also dangerous.

questions.question: Passing and being passed on a motorcycle is similar to a car. However:

options.text: Being seen is more important for a motorcycle than for a car.
Being seen is less important for a motorcycle than for a car.
You should pass on the shoulder instead of on the main road.
You must make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Being seen is more important for a motorcycle than for a car.
questions.explanation: Being seen is critical when riding a motorcycle. Motorcycles are smaller and easier to miss. Other drivers may not see you even if they are looking, or you may disappear into their blind spot.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a turn too fast?

options.text: You might end up in another lane of traffic.
You will get through the turn faster.
You will keep better control of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You might end up in another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast may cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before entering a turn or curve.

questions.question: A motorcyclist can stop other vehicles from sharing their lane by:

options.text: Riding on the left side of the lane.
Riding in the center of the lane.
Making angry gestures at other drivers.
Riding in a zigzag pattern across the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when other drivers might try to squeeze in next to you. This position discourages them from sharing your lane.

questions.question: When riding over rough surfaces, you should:

options.text: Hold the handgrips loosely to let your arms move.
Hold the handgrips firmly to stay in control.
Use a lot of throttle to get over the rough area.
Ride without a helmet so it does not cover your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handgrips firmly to stay in control.
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly when riding over rough surfaces. This keeps your motorcycle pointed in the right direction.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, you should:

options.text: Stay on the right side of your lane.
Stay on the left side of your lane.
Look to your left often.
Check your mirrors more than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay on the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay away from parked cars when passing them. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out between the cars.

questions.question: A good lane position helps you do all of the following, except:

options.text: Avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Be seen better.
Go faster.
Get ready for turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go faster.
questions.explanation: Your lane position helps you see and be seen better, avoid blind spots, and prepare for turns. However, it does not help you go faster.

questions.question: A load on your motorcycle should be placed:

options.text: As low as possible.
As high as possible.
Behind the rear axle.
On one side of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them in saddlebags or tie them down. Placing loads high on the back can raise your motorcycle's center of gravity and throw off the balance. Always distribute loads equally on both sides.

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Let them pass.
Prevent them from passing.
Move to one side of your lane to let them share it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up will only increase danger.

questions.question: A danger of braking too hard is:

options.text: Losing grip on one or both wheels.
Stopping too soon.
Popping a tire.
Taking too long to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing grip on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: Braking too hard can cause you to lose traction and crash.

questions.question: During the day, you should:

options.text: Not ride with your headlight on.
Ride with your headlight on only when it is cloudy.
Always ride with your headlight on.
Use your headlight if you want to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Always keep your headlight on when riding, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to see you.

questions.question: All of the following reduce accident risk, except:

options.text: Staying alert.
Spotting hazards and planning how to deal with them.
Riding without a headlight.
Keeping space around your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding without a headlight.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, stay alert and watch for hazards. Spot dangers and decide what to handle first. Always use your headlight to be more visible and keep plenty of space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:

options.text: Never.
Only during the day.
Only at night.
Day and night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Day and night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Wear bright colors and reflective clothing at all times to make yourself more visible.

questions.question: Hearing protection should be:

options.text: Not used.
Used only on long rides.
Used on every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Used on every ride.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a helmet. Use hearing protection every time you ride to protect your hearing.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
Never hold onto the rider.
Not lean into turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to hold firmly onto your hips, waist, or belt before you start riding. They can also hold onto secure handholds if they are available.

questions.question: A person of legal drinking age is considered legally intoxicated with a blood alcohol level (PAC) of _____ or higher.

options.text: 0.08 percent
0.04 percent
0.1 percent
0.15 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A blood alcohol level of 0.08 percent means you are legally intoxicated. Riding a motorcycle while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When should a rider use their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly
When stopped at an intersection
When changing lanes
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down or stopping, when stopped at intersections, when changing lanes, and when turning.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, the safest approach is to:

options.text: Go straight ahead in your lane.
Approach at a 45-degree angle.
Approach at a 90-degree angle.
Cross at a fast speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight ahead in your lane.
questions.explanation: Go straight ahead in your lane when crossing angled railroad tracks. Turning to cross at a right angle can be dangerous because it may push you into another lane.

questions.question: After entering a turn, you should give the throttle gas and:

options.text: Always slow down.
Keep your speed steady or speed up slowly.
Speed up quickly.
Not worry about your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your speed steady or speed up slowly.
questions.explanation: Apply the throttle smoothly through a turn to keep your suspension stable. Keep your speed steady or increase it slowly through the turn.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should NOT:

options.text: Choose a lane position that makes them more visible.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Cover the clutch and brakes to react faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that other drivers can see clearly. Cover your clutch and both brakes to react faster. Slow down as you approach an intersection. Do not change your speed or position suddenly because other drivers may not understand what you are doing.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Parking spaces reserved for people with disabilities.
Slow-moving vehicle.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parking spaces reserved for people with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces for vehicles with disability license plates, disabled veteran plates, or disability parking placards.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: Your mirrors show you everything around you.
Turn your head to check blind spots in addition to using mirrors.
Signal and move immediately to the right or left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check blind spots in addition to using mirrors.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, in addition to using your mirrors.

questions.question: This is a __________ sign.

options.text: Stop
Wrong way
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield
questions.explanation: Triangular signs pointing downward mean you must yield. When you see a yield sign, slow down to a safe speed for the conditions and stop if needed. Stop at a marked stop line if one exists.
